transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lowe (Redwood SE), Priya Mehta (Colossus Legal), Daniel Ortiz (Colossus Head of IT), Sasha Nguyen (Colossus Security), Liam Park (Colossus Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick procurement/msa/dpa review, clarify SLAs, agree pilot timeline and deliverables

00:00 Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Avery from Redwood - I think you all can hear me?
00:05 Priya Mehta: Yes thanks, can hear you. We'll do the legal bits first, then technical, then procurement timeline.
00:12 Marcus Lowe: Hi all - Marcus from Redwood infra, I'll handle the SLA and performance questions.

00:35 Priya Mehta: We sent initial redlines on the MSA and the DPA last week. Main concerns are liability cap, indemnity, and data residency clauses. Also need clarity on audit logs and retention.
00:48 Avery Chen: Totally, thank you. On the liability cap we usually default to our standard language but we're open to discussion for enterprise. Can you highlight the specific clause you want changed?
01:10 Priya Mehta: It's section 9 - the cap is at one million currently; our legal prefers six months of fees or a lower multiple. We also want stronger breach notification timelines - 48 hours instead of 72.
01:28 Avery Chen: Understood. We can propose a middle ground. We'll send redlines that map to your ask.

02:02 Daniel Ortiz: From an IT perspective, we need to confirm VPC peering and KMS integration. Is Redwood Private an option or do we need Dedicated?
02:16 Marcus Lowe: Good question. For the pilot you can go hosted while we validate throughput; if you need tenant isolation and private networking we offer Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). There was a note in the DPA about customer-managed KMS and HSM - we support KMS integrations with Bring-Your-Own keys for Dedicated and Private.
02:42 Sasha Nguyen: The transcription I saw earlier said "Red wood Dedicate" - sorry that's a little off - but we need to confirm key rotation policies and that keys never leave customer control. Also SOC2/ISO evidence.
02:58 Marcus Lowe: Right, keys stay under customer control when you enable BYOK. We use envelope encryption at rest and TLS in transit. I'll send our SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts.

03:20 Priya Mehta: Also need to confirm data processing - do model outputs ever leave the customer's region? Our contract requires EU data residency for EU tenants.
03:34 Avery Chen: We can pin region routing. For hosted customers we route requests to region endpoints; for Dedicated we can provision in their region or on-prem. We'll add a clause to the DPA to reflect region residency guarantees for the pilot.

04:05 Liam Park: On pricing: procurement wants a clear dedicated capacity SKU and a pilot pricing schedule. We need monthly commit pricing, burst pricing, and overage rates. Also want to see sample invoice layout for PO approvals.
04:26 Avery Chen: We'll send the dedicated pricing sheet and sample invoice. For pilot, we usually do a 30-day pilot with metered hosted credits or a small reserved commitment. What budget window are you targeting?
04:42 Liam Park: We're budgeting this quarter, want sign-off by end of month. So pilot kickoff ideally next week, full procurement by 10/22.

05:15 Marcus Lowe: From the SLA side - for Dedicated we can offer a 99.9% uptime target, token latency SLOs depend on model and sequence length. For example, for the LLM-13B family on a standard p4-equivalent Dedicated node we see median generation latency ~120-180ms for 64-token responses. Benchmarks vary.
05:42 Daniel Ortiz: That 120-180ms - is that single-request median or under load? Our workload will have bursts and steady ingestion.
05:53 Marcus Lowe: Median under steady-state, with continuous batching enabled. Under bursty traffic we recommend autoscale policies, which we can configure. For predictable latency at scale we recommend a reserved Dedicated pool. We'll include a benchmark report with tail-latency percentiles.

06:20 Priya Mehta: Back to legal - DPA: can you confirm subprocessors list and ability to add/remove? We need 30-day notice for subprocessor changes.
06:34 Avery Chen: Yes, subprocessors are listed in the data processing appendix; we provide notice for changes. For Dedicated we can offer more control over subprocessors since some services are customer-managed.

07:00 Sasha Nguyen: On auditing: we need logs for all admin actions and model access, with 365-day retention. Is that standard?
07:12 Marcus Lowe: Default retention is 90 days on hosted; enterprise add-on can be 365 days. For Dedicated you can configure log sinks to your SIEM and we can extend retention as part of the contract.

07:35 Priya Mehta: About indemnity: we need clearer product/service definitions - what's considered misuse vs proper use. Also openAI-style output risk - who is liable for hallucinations?
07:54 Avery Chen: Typically the customer is responsible for how outputs are used. We can add language to clarify expected use and a mutual indemnity carve-out for third-party IP claims, standard industry language. We'll propose text to address hallucination risk allocation.

08:25 Liam Park: Who signs the SOW for the pilot? AE or Solutions Engineer? We need an SOW that references MSA and DPA.
08:34 Avery Chen: We'll issue a pilot SOW referencing the MSA and DPA; I'll be the signatory on Redwood's side, and we'll include scope, acceptance criteria, and pricing.

09:00 Priya Mehta: Are there any penalties or credits for SLA misses? We saw references to credits in the SLA.
09:08 Marcus Lowe: For hosted we offer service credits tiers based on monthly uptime. For Dedicated we can negotiate service credits and response times in the SLA. We'll include proposed credit tables in the SLA attachment.

09:45 Daniel Ortiz: On security reviews - will you provide a penetration test report or allow us to run a security assessment in a sandbox?
09:53 Avery Chen: We can share third-party pentest and our remediation summary. For Dedicated or Private we can enable a sandbox environment for your security team to run scans under an NDA. We'll coordinate with security.

10:20 Sasha Nguyen: Also need SSO/SAML and RBAC. How granular is your RBAC?
10:28 Marcus Lowe: RBAC supports per-route and per-project roles - admin, dev, viewer - and token scoping so you can restrict model invocation. We also have audit logs for token usage.

10:50 Priya Mehta: Fine, so next from legal side: we'll mark up the MSA and DPA with redlines and then expect Redwood's redline back.
10:58 Avery Chen: Yes, we'll send our redlined MSA to you by EOD Friday 10/15.

11:30 Liam Park: Quick question on data retention: if we terminate, what is data return/deletion process? We need cert of deletion timeline.
11:42 Marcus Lowe: We provide data export and deletion APIs. Standard timeframe is 30 days to purge backups and provide a deletion certificate; we can shorten as negotiated in the DPA.

12:10 Priya Mehta: Looking at the DPA, there's a section about model training. We need to ensure Colossus data won't be used to train public models.
12:21 Avery Chen: We do not use customer data for model training unless explicitly opted in. We'll add explicit language to the DPA confirming no training on customer payloads.

12:45 Daniel Ortiz: For the pilot, we want to test a reranking pipeline and embeddings. Any constraints on batch sizes?
12:56 Marcus Lowe: Embeddings are typically CPU/GPU depending on model; we'll give recommended batch sizing. For reranking, we'll show throughput numbers and cost per 1k queries in the pricing sheet.

13:30 Priya Mehta: On international privacy, if we have EU PHI there's extra compliance. Can you support EU-hosted Dedicated instances?
13:44 Avery Chen: Yes, we have EU region deployments for Dedicated and Private. We'll add a clause guaranteeing EU residency for that workload.

14:10 Liam Park: Procurement needs a sample PO and payment terms - net30? net45?
14:18 Avery Chen: Standard is net30; we can discuss net45 for larger SOWs. We'll include sample invoice and payment terms.

14:50 Priya Mehta: One more legal item: we require audit rights for SOC2 in the contract - is that feasible?
14:58 Avery Chen: We provide SOC2 reports and allow auditor access under standard controls and NDAs. We'll include language in the MSA.

15:30 Marcus Lowe: I can do a short demo of the Dedicated dashboard after this call if the team wants - show autoscale and routing policies.
15:40 Daniel Ortiz: That would be helpful - especially how fallbacks are configured.

16:05 Marcus Lowe: Quick note on fallbacks - requests can be routed by policy (latency, cost, region), and we've got automatic fallback to compatible smaller model variants when capacity is constrained. Demo will show policy UI.

16:55 Priya Mehta: Ok that helps. Any blockers on our side for moving forward?
17:05 Liam Park: Budget sign-off and legal review timelines. If legal returns redlines by 10/19 and procurement confirms funding by 10/22 we can proceed with SOW and pilot.

17:30 Avery Chen: Recap of next steps: we'll send redlined MSA (Avery), benchmark and SLA details (Marcus), SOC2/ISO docs (Marcus), dedicated pricing sheet and invoice sample (Avery). Proposed pilot kickoff 2026-10-20.
17:52 Priya Mehta: Sounds good. I'll aim to have legal redlines by 10/19.

18:20 Daniel Ortiz: For the technical checks, my team will schedule a 30-minute deep dive on environment connectivity next week.
18:30 Marcus Lowe: I'll set that up and bring network diagrams.

19:00 Liam Park: One small ask - can you include an escalation matrix in the SLA with named contacts and response times?
19:10 Avery Chen: Yes we'll include an escalation matrix as an SLA appendix.

19:30 Priya Mehta: Thanks all. Anything else?
19:35 Avery Chen: Nothing else. Thanks for your time. We'll follow up with docs and a redline by 10/15.

End of transcript.
